title: In Korea, the Dream Home Is an Apartment

slides.headline: In Korea, the dream home is **an apartment.**
slides.note: Not a house with a yard. A unit on the 15th floor.

slides.headline: More than half **live in one**
slides.body: Over half of Korean households live in an apartment (아파트), and about 6 in 10 homes are apartment units.

slides.headline: Built fast. **Built tall.**
slides.body: From the 1970s, millions moved from farms to cities. Rows of identical towers were the quickest way to house them.

slides.headline: A town **inside the gates**
slides.body: A complex (단지) has its own playgrounds, gyms, parking and management office. Some hold thousands of homes.

slides.headline: Giant numbers **on every tower**
slides.body: Each building gets a number like 101 or 102, painted huge on its side. An address ends in building and unit: 101-1502.

slides.headline: Not the cheap option. **The goal.**
slides.body: In many countries, tower blocks mean public housing. In Korea, a new apartment from a big-name builder is what people save for.

slides.headline: Your complex **says something**
slides.body: Which complex you live in can work like a résumé. Kids from rental blocks have been teased for it.

slides.headline: Average price of **a Seoul apartment**
slides.body: Over US$700,000. For many families, the apartment is most of what they own.

slides.headline: Safe and warm. **And all the same.**
slides.body: A French geographer called Korea a "Republic of Apartments." Fans point to security, floor heating and city access.

slides.headline: Korea, explained **by a Korean.**
slides.body: Follow for the context behind the things Korea does.
slides.graphic: Seoul apartment complex at dusk, softly blurred behind the text.
slides.design_note: Use the account's established CTA treatment and amber highlight.

caption:
In Korea, more than half of households live in an apartment, and a new one is the home most families dream of.

Whole towns sit inside gated complexes, every tower wears a giant number, and in Seoul the average unit sells for over ₩1 billion.

Where you live, is an apartment the dream or the fallback?
reply: One more: the word is so Korean that ROSÉ and Bruno Mars named a 2024 global hit "APT." It comes from a drinking game chant, and a 1982 song called "Apartment" was already a singalong classic. Ask a Korean where they live and you may hear the complex name before the neighborhood. Do people where you live want a house, or an apartment?
fact_check: 2장: 인구주택총조사 아파트 거주 가구 비율 2020년 51.5%로 첫 과반, 이후 상승. 전체 주택 중 아파트 약 64%(2023 주택총조사) — 발행 전 최신 통계 확인.
3장: 1960~70년대 이촌향도·도시화, 1962 마포아파트 첫 단지형, 1970년대 강남 개발·1989 주택 200만호 계획.
5장: 동·호수 표기(101동 1502호), 외벽 동 번호 대형 표기.
7장: 임대 단지 아동 차별('휴거' 등) 언론 보도 다수.
8장: KB부동산 서울 아파트 평균 매매가 10억 원 이상(2021년 이후), 환율 약 1,350~1,400원.
